tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the Pali Canon on dhamma.gift by keyword/substring or REGEX (min 3 letters, no semantic search). Patterns like "kata.*dukkha", "vucc.*dukkha", "katha.*dukkha" find the canon's own definitions and expositions of a term. Returns a CENSUS of every matching sutta — id, title, match count, metaphor count, reader link — Pali only, ordered so that suttas that DEFINE the term come first, then ones NAMED after it, then by how often it occurs. Set include_segments for the matched Pali lines, include_translations (+ langs) for translations. 40 suttas by default (25 by occurrence count, plus 15 for suttas named after the term and ones defining it); metadata.totalFiles reports the true count, and limit takes a number or "all".

query.description: Keyword, phrase, or REGEX pattern to search for (Pali or a translation word). Patterns work and are the way to find definitions: "kata.*dukkha" (Katamañca … dukkhaṁ?), "vucc.*dukkha" (idaṁ vuccati dukkhaṁ), "katha.*dukkha" (Kathañca … hoti?).

scope.description: default|all|dhamma|vinaya|abhi|khudakka|or comma-separated nikaya codes (dn,mn,...). Default: default (4 nikayas + 6 KN books).

langs.description: Translation languages to include with include_translations, e.g. ["ru","en"]. Default: none (Pali only).

translators.description: Explicit translator keys, e.g. ["en_sujato"] to include Sujato, or ["ru_sv"]. Needed only to override the default translator choice.

include_segments.description: Also return the matched Pali segments (segment id, text, reader link). Default: false — the census alone.

include_translations.description: Also return translations of the matched segments (implies include_segments). Default: false.

limit.description: How many suttas to list: a number, or "all" for every match. Default: 40, composed of 25 by occurrence count plus 15 for suttas named after the term and defining it. Strict — the cap means the cap. metadata.totalFiles always carries the true match count, so a truncated answer still tells you how much more there is. Suttas whose TITLE matches the query rank first within their collection.

tools.name: get_text
tools.description: Fetch a sutta by id (e.g. "dn22", "mn1", "sn56.11") — the Pali text (Mahāsaṅgīti) of every segment. Pali only by default; pass langs for translations, translators to name a translator (e.g. ["en_sujato"]), editions for the whole text of other Pali editions line by line (the whole canon, see compare_editions). Same data as dhamma.gift/api/text.

editions.description: Other Pali editions to add, each segment beside the Mahāsaṅgīti: bjt (Buddha Jayanti, Sri Lanka), my (Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana, Myanmar), th (Siam Rath, Thailand), mso (Mahāsaṅgīti as printed, 2005), pts (Pali Text Society), or ["all"]. The whole canon (gaps: https://dhamma.gift/docs/compare).

suttaId.description: Sutta id, e.g. dn22, mn1, sn56.11.

langs.description: Translation languages to include, e.g. ["ru","en"]. Default: none (Pali only).

translators.description: Explicit translator keys, e.g. ["en_sujato"] to include Sujato.

tools.name: compare_editions
tools.description: Compare the Pali Canon's editions line by line: the Mahāsaṅgīti beside Buddha Jayanti (Sri Lanka), Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana (Myanmar), Siam Rath (Thailand), the printed Mahāsaṅgīti of 2005 and the PTS editions (the whole canon; gaps: PTS has no Netti or Peṭakopadesa, of the Jātaka the verses only, of the later books only what PTS printed; Siam Rath has no Pātimokkha (the Mahāmakuṭa Pātimokkha stands in its place, pli-tv-bu-pm); the Mahāsaṅgīti of 2005 lacks a few passages of the later books. Details: https://dhamma.gift/docs/compare). Give a sutta ("sn56.11"), a line ("dn22:18.1") or a range ("sn56.11:5.1-5.4"). The answer starts with a summary per edition (name, license, lines present, missing, differing), then the lines where some edition reads differently, each with the differing words. Case, punctuation and ṁ/ṃ are not counted as differences.

id.description: A sutta (sn56.11), a line (dn22:18.1) or a range of lines (sn56.11:5.1-5.4).

editions.description: Editions to compare with the Mahāsaṅgīti. Default: all of bjt, my, th, mso, pts.

all.description: Every line, not only the lines where an edition differs. Default false.

limit.description: Lines per answer (default 60); the answer gives next_from to continue.

from.description: Continue from this line (the next_from of a previous answer).

tools.name: compare_translations
tools.description: One segment of the canon in the Pali root and every available translation side by side. Use a segment id from search/get_text, e.g. "mn129:21.3". Sujato (en_sujato) is excluded unless named in translators.

segmentId.description: Segment id as returned by search, e.g. mn129:21.3 or dn22:1.1.

langs.description: Limit to these languages, e.g. ["ru","en"]. Default: all.

translators.description: Explicit translator keys, e.g. ["en_sujato"] to include Sujato.

tools.name: list_structure
tools.description: What texts exist. Without arguments: collections (sutta/vinaya/abhidhamma/khuddaka), books by id prefix with sutta counts, and translation languages with translators. With prefix (e.g. "mn", "sn56", "an4"): the suttas under it with titles.

prefix.description: Sutta id prefix such as mn, sn56, an4, dhp. Max 200 suttas are listed.

tools.name: uposatha
tools.description: Uposatha days by the Suttas (the 8th, 14th/15th of each half-month, by the real moon) for the next N days at a place, the same engine as dhamma.gift/uposatha-calendar, the Uposatha app and the Telegram bot. The day runs from sunset to sunset at the place: each row gives its begin (sunset of the eve), dawn, noon and end times. Without coordinates: Bodh Gaya. Give lat/lon and the IANA time zone of the user's city for local times.

tz.description: IANA time zone of the place, e.g. "Asia/Bangkok". Needed with lat/lon.

place.description: Name of the place, echoed back.

lang.description: Language of the day names. Default: en.

tools.name: dictionary
tools.description: Look a word up in the Dictionary of dhamma.gift (dict.dhamma.gift): (1) dg — the project's glossary: where the Suttas and the Vinaya DEFINE the term (the Pali definition line and its segment ids), broader uses, Vinaya uses, and similes/metaphors (adhivacana, upamā, seyyathāpi) built on it; (2) dpd — the Digital Pali Dictionary meanings for the form (the headwords it may come from, with DG's own definition refs merged in); (3) sanskrit — 20+ Sanskrit dictionaries of the Cologne Digital Sanskrit Lexicon (Monier-Williams, Edgerton's Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit, Apte, Böhtlingk-Roth…) through their API. Give the Pali form as it stands in the text; for Sanskrit give its Sanskrit form in IAST (dukkha → duḥkha, dhamma → dharma) as sanskrit_word.

word.description: The Pali word, IAST with diacritics (dukkha, taṇhā, upādāna), any inflected form.

sanskrit_word.description: The Sanskrit form in IAST for the Sanskrit dictionaries (duḥkha, tṛṣṇā). Default: word.

lang.description: Language of the glossary renderings and DPD meanings. Default: en.
